Executive takeaway

Strong evidence

Efficiency edge

BBVA has a credible claim to world-class profitability and efficiency. A claim to world's best bank overall is not yet demonstrated.

Governance, controls, resilience and execution.

KPI dictionary: 24 priority indicators

Business / earnings / efficiency

Market share · gross loans · deposits · loan CAGR · geography concentration · RoTE (reported) · RoA · pre-provision profit/RWA · 5-year earnings volatility · organic CET1 generation · cost/income · cost/assets · revenue–cost jaws.

Financial resilience

Gross NPL ratio · cost of risk · Stage 2 / loans · CET1 ratio · leverage ratio · regulatory headroom · LCR · NSFR · loan/deposit · customer-deposit funding share.

Qualitative evidence adds customer satisfaction, digital outcomes, governance and strategic execution. They require separate rubric-based evaluation.

Definitions: RoTE = profit attributable to ordinary shareholders / average tangible common equity; cost/income = operating expenses / operating income; CET1 = CET1 capital / RWA. Bank-reported values may diverge because of denominator, adjustment, consolidation and accounting treatments.

Data-quality rules

Source hierarchy

  1. Audited filings and regulatory disclosures
  2. Official FY results and investor presentations
  3. EBA / other supervisory databases
  4. Ratings methodologies, market surveys and awards for context

Comparability safeguards

  • Keep RoTE, ROTCE, ROE separate
  • Do not equate regulatory CET1 across jurisdictions
  • Do not equate gross and net NPL ratios
  • Distinguish stated vs adjusted/recurring profit
  • Do not combine FY2025 and 9M2026 in rankings

No missing observations have been estimated or silently filled. Coverage and sample size accompany every ranking.

RoTE-only comparison. 14 banks reported the metric in the sourced snapshot; US ROTCE and banks reporting only ROE are excluded.

2025: cost efficiency comparison

Lower cost/income generally indicates better operating efficiency, but business mix, one-offs and local presentation matter.

Illustrative issuer-reported cost/income ratios. BBVA ranks 4/20 among 20 sourced values (including non-European banks). ICBC and Banorte have different business mix and accounting context.

2025: capital ratio is not a league table

Why not rank banks by CET1 alone?

Risk weights, model permissions, regulatory floors and capital expectations vary across jurisdictions. A higher CET1 ratio may coexist with a riskier portfolio, lower leverage capital or different minimum requirements.

BBVA reported 12.70% at FY2025, compared with 14.75% for UniCredit and 14.6% (US standardized) for JPMorgan.

CaixaBank figure reflects a particular regulatory distribution treatment; Lloyds is pro forma. These are not on an identical basis.

FY2025 NPL ratio; Singapore-based business mix.

Illustrative question

Does BBVA’s higher profitability sufficiently compensate for its higher loan-loss experience and emerging-market risk? A direct comparison requires loan segmentation, portfolio mix, expected-loss calibration and macroeconomic adjustments.

Gross NPL, net NPL and Stage 3 metrics are not interchangeable. Do not score missing risk data as zero.

A crucial difference: bank model and geography

BBVA’s distinct exposure

Material Mexico, Türkiye and South America exposure increases geographic diversification but also introduces inflation, FX, credit and sovereign-risk considerations.

For example, FY2025 group cost of risk was 1.39%, versus 0.34% in BBVA Spain and 3.31% in BBVA Mexico.

Comparison principles

  • Consolidated-bank ranking for the headline
  • Geographic/segment peer tests to diagnose differences
  • Risk-adjusted return before claiming economic superiority
  • Separate IFRS, US GAAP and local capital regimes

Source: BBVA FY2025 results; rating-agency operating-environment methodologies.

Four dimensions still resist numeric ranking

Franchise

Use domestic market share, deposit durability, concentration, diversification and customer growth. Group assets alone reward size, not excellence.

Customers

Country-specific external NPS/satisfaction panels, product value, service reliability, dispute metrics. Raw self-reported NPS is not globally comparable.

Technology

Digital unit economics and cost savings, digital adoption with normalized definitions, reliability and fraud outcomes. Awards are supporting evidence.

Governance

Verified regulatory actions, risk controls, operational incidents, strategy delivery and board oversight; distinguish ratings from governance assessment.

No unsupported qualitative scores or award-count league table have been invented for these categories.

Sensitivity: what can we honestly claim?

Scenario A

Prioritize operating excellence

BBVA is near the top on sourced RoTE and cost/income. Some competitors (e.g., Intesa on RoTE, UniCredit on C/I) match or exceed it.

Scenario B

Prioritize financial resilience

Conclusion becomes less clear; capital, NPL, funding and operating country risk must be normalized.

Scenario C

Prioritize customer and digital outcomes

Evidence is not comparable enough for a defensible winner — rankings withheld.

Robust conclusion: BBVA is a strong contender.
Not robust: BBVA is definitively #1 worldwide.

Verdict: evidence versus ambition

EVIDENCE SUPPORTS
  • Elite FY2025 profitability within its own peer set
  • Very strong cost efficiency
  • Strong 9M2026 reported momentum
  • Coherent commercial banking and digital strategy
NOT YET ESTABLISHED
  • Full risk-adjusted superiority
  • Top global liquidity / capital / asset quality position
  • Independent global customer-experience leadership
  • Complete 2021–2025 consistency test
  • Defensible composite nine-dimension #1 score
BBVA belongs in the conversation about the world's best banks — but the evidence supports a qualified, not absolute, verdict.

Next evidence required to finish the ranking

Priority 1 · Comparable quantitative panel

  1. 23 banks × 2021–2025 core raw data
  2. Normalize ordinary earnings, capital basis, loan quality
  3. Document cross-border prudential adjustments
  4. Compute peer-level and pooled statistics

Priority 2 · Independent qualitative panel

  1. Customer surveys by market and product
  2. Digital outcomes on common units
  3. Verified management / governance events
  4. Blind scoring rubric with audit trail

No input is needed to use this presentation. To complete a full quantitative ranking faster, access to a licensed, bank-level dataset (e.g., The Banker or S&P Capital IQ) would materially help.
